learningObjective: Choose where billable-mass calculation belongs when callers must share one result derived from shipment measures and carrier class.

question.prompt: A parcel quote has 3 measured dimensions and a carrier class divisor. The quoted billable mass is used by two callers; neither caller owns measurement rules. Choose where billable-mass calculation belongs when callers must share one result derived from shipment measures and carrier class.

options.text: Let the ParcelQuote calculate billable mass from its dimensions and selected carrier class.
Have each checkout caller calculate billable mass from the exposed dimensions.
Store billable mass as an independently editable field beside the dimensions.

feedback.reason: Place a calculation with the cohesive information it needs, rather than duplicating it in callers. In this case, Let the ParcelQuote calculate billable mass from its dimensions and selected carrier class.

details.mechanismOrProperty: ParcelQuote owns both the measures and carrier-class choice used by this derived value.
details.scenarioApplication: Both callers now obtain the same quote calculation from the object that has all required inputs.
details.errorCorrection: A second caller can use a different rounding or divisor rule, so identical parcel state can yield conflicting quotes. The saved number can drift from the measures after an amendment.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If carrier policy becomes independently versioned, inject a policy value; do not duplicate the arithmetic in each caller.
details.transfer: Keep a derived rule with its complete input state unless the scenario establishes a separate policy owner.

messages.text: A second caller can use a different rounding or divisor rule, so identical parcel state can yield conflicting quotes.
The saved number can drift from the measures after an amendment.

learningObjective: Choose how the session should report remaining places when confirmation status changes.

question.prompt: A workshop session stores confirmed attendee IDs and has a visible capacity. Waitlisted people are not confirmed. Choose how the session should report remaining places when confirmation status changes.

options.text: Maintain a separate remainingPlaces counter that each registration caller increments or decrements.
Ask the dashboard to count every attendee record, including waitlisted people.
Have WorkshopSession compute remaining places from its confirmed attendee set and capacity.

feedback.reason: Derive a summary from the authoritative membership state it describes. In this case, Have WorkshopSession compute remaining places from its confirmed attendee set and capacity.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The session already owns both capacity and confirmed membership.
details.scenarioApplication: Remaining capacity changes whenever a person becomes or ceases to be confirmed.
details.errorCorrection: A cancellation path can update membership but miss the counter, so the displayed number no longer describes the stored attendees. That count includes people who do not consume a confirmed place under the stated rule.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A reporting projection may cache the result, but its source must remain this confirmed-membership rule.
details.transfer: A summary should be derived at the boundary that owns the facts defining it.

messages.text: A cancellation path can update membership but miss the counter, so the displayed number no longer describes the stored attendees.
That count includes people who do not consume a confirmed place under the stated rule.

learningObjective: Choose how an issued line should calculate its amount after catalog prices change.

question.prompt: An invoice line captures quantity and unit price at issue time. The catalog price may later change; old invoices must still show the issued amount. Choose how an issued line should calculate its amount after catalog prices change.

options.text: Copy the invoice amount into every screen-specific presenter and treat each copy as authoritative.
Let InvoiceLine compute its amount from its captured quantity and unit price.
Re-read today’s catalog price whenever an old invoice is displayed.

feedback.reason: Keep historical behavior cohesive with the state captured by the historical object. In this case, Let InvoiceLine compute its amount from its captured quantity and unit price.

details.mechanismOrProperty: InvoiceLine has the exact captured values that define this historical amount.
details.scenarioApplication: Catalog edits affect future lines while the old line continues to show its issued amount.
details.errorCorrection: That substitutes current catalog state for the values the issued line captured. The same issued line can then display different totals depending on which screen recalculated it.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A tax policy can remain an explicit collaborator if the invoice also captures the applicable policy version.
details.transfer: Place behavior with the state that gives the behavior its meaning, especially when that state is historical.

messages.text: The same issued line can then display different totals depending on which screen recalculated it.
That substitutes current catalog state for the values the issued line captured.

learningObjective: Choose where scaling belongs so one batch can change without altering the master recipe.

question.prompt: A recipe batch stores ingredient quantities for its selected serving count. The master recipe remains unchanged when a cook scales one batch. Choose where scaling belongs so one batch can change without altering the master recipe.

options.text: Let RecipeBatch calculate its ingredient quantities from its own serving count and the selected recipe revision.
Let the recipe editor overwrite master quantities each time a cook changes serving count.
Let each shopping-list screen independently multiply the master values by the requested servings.

feedback.reason: Distinguish batch-specific state from its source definition when assigning behavior. In this case, Let RecipeBatch calculate its ingredient quantities from its own serving count and the selected recipe revision.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The batch owns the chosen serving count and selected source revision.
details.scenarioApplication: A second batch can scale independently while both retain the same master recipe.
details.errorCorrection: That edits the reusable definition when only one prepared batch is changing. Different consumers can apply different rounding and forget batch-specific adjustments.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a recipe revision changes, use its explicit revision rather than mutating batches already prepared from an earlier one.
details.transfer: Attach a calculation to the object whose local state controls the result, not merely the object from which it originated.

messages.text: That edits the reusable definition when only one prepared batch is changing.
Different consumers can apply different rounding and forget batch-specific adjustments.

learningObjective: Choose how the playlist should expose its total runtime when tracks are reordered or replaced.

question.prompt: A playlist stores an ordered set of tracks. Track durations come from the playlist’s selected track versions; duration is not manually editable. Choose how the playlist should expose its total runtime when tracks are reordered or replaced.

options.text: Persist a second editable runtime field and update it from each reorder screen.
Have each playback screen sum whichever current track versions its own cache returns.
Have Playlist compute runtime from its ordered selected track versions.

feedback.reason: Keep an aggregate derived from owned members aligned with their ordering and versions. In this case, Have Playlist compute runtime from its ordered selected track versions.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The playlist owns the ordered membership and selected versions used by the total.
details.scenarioApplication: Replacing a selected track version changes runtime; reordering the same tracks preserves the total while changing playback order.
details.errorCorrection: A track replacement can leave that independent field inconsistent with the actual list. The playlist’s displayed runtime can depend on unrelated cache freshness instead of its selected members.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A separately materialized search index may lag, but it should be labeled as a projection rather than the playlist’s authoritative runtime.
details.transfer: When a value describes an object’s current members, derive it from those members at the owner boundary.

messages.text: A track replacement can leave that independent field inconsistent with the actual list.
The playlist’s displayed runtime can depend on unrelated cache freshness instead of its selected members.

learningObjective: Choose how a historical corrected value should be obtained after the device is recalibrated.

question.prompt: A sensor reading stores the raw measurement and the calibration revision used when it was taken. Later recalibration must not rewrite historical readings. Choose how a historical corrected value should be obtained after the device is recalibrated.

options.text: Let the chart and export each maintain their own corrected-value formula.
Have SensorReading apply its captured calibration revision to its raw measurement.
Apply whichever calibration is currently active whenever any screen opens the old reading.

feedback.reason: Keep historical interpretation tied to the measurement’s captured calibration state. In this case, Have SensorReading apply its captured calibration revision to its raw measurement.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The reading owns the raw value and the calibration revision that gives it historical meaning.
details.scenarioApplication: Recalibration changes future readings while archived readings retain their prior interpretation.
details.errorCorrection: That reinterprets an old measurement using state that did not apply when it was captured. Independent formulas can disagree about the same archived reading.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If policy requires restating history, model that as an explicit restatement instead of silently changing display behavior.
details.transfer: Use the state that defines a historical result as part of the object that represents that result.

messages.text: Independent formulas can disagree about the same archived reading.
That reinterprets an old measurement using state that did not apply when it was captured.

learningObjective: Choose how the allowance should expose its remaining accepted balance.

question.prompt: A monthly allowance stores a period limit and accepted charges for that period. Draft charges do not reduce available balance. Choose how the allowance should expose its remaining accepted balance.

options.text: Let MonthlyAllowance subtract its accepted charges from its period limit.
Keep a cached balance that every charge editor changes before the charge is accepted.
Have each account page subtract all visible charges, including drafts.

feedback.reason: Calculate a balance from the exact set of state that counts toward it. In this case, Let MonthlyAllowance subtract its accepted charges from its period limit.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The allowance owns the period limit and the accepted-charge membership.
details.scenarioApplication: Accepting or reversing a charge changes the balance through the same domain rule.
details.errorCorrection: A rejected draft could reduce the balance despite not being part of accepted charges. The display would include records excluded by the allowance’s stated accounting state.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A ledger may independently record accounting entries, but the allowance balance must use the defined accepted set.
details.transfer: Choose the authoritative state set first, then keep its derived balance rule alongside that state.

messages.text: A rejected draft could reduce the balance despite not being part of accepted charges.
The display would include records excluded by the allowance’s stated accounting state.

learningObjective: Choose how bounds validation should stay consistent across preview and export.

question.prompt: A crop stores an image size and a rectangle. A crop must remain inside the image; the editor previews the same rectangle that export uses. Choose how bounds validation should stay consistent across preview and export.

options.text: Let the preview component check bounds while export accepts any rectangle it receives.
Allow callers to mutate rectangle coordinates directly and repair them on the next render.
Have ImageCrop validate a proposed rectangle against its stored image dimensions.

feedback.reason: Place a state-dependent validity check with the object whose dimensions define validity. In this case, Have ImageCrop validate a proposed rectangle against its stored image dimensions.

details.mechanismOrProperty: ImageCrop has both the rectangle and the image dimensions needed for the check.
details.scenarioApplication: Both preview and export can use the same valid crop state.
details.errorCorrection: The two paths can disagree because only one protects the stated geometry. The object can persist an invalid crop before that later render occurs.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A separate image decoder may validate file format, but it does not replace this geometric check.
details.transfer: Keep a check with the state that defines whether the state is valid.

messages.text: The two paths can disagree because only one protects the stated geometry.
The object can persist an invalid crop before that later render occurs.

learningObjective: Choose how meeting duration should be calculated for attendees in different zones.

question.prompt: A meeting stores start and end instants. Each attendee sees those instants in their own time zone; the event does not store a single local wall-clock label. Choose how meeting duration should be calculated for attendees in different zones.

options.text: Store a separate duration that organizers can edit independently of both instants.
Have Meeting calculate elapsed duration from its stored start and end instants.
Subtract each attendee’s locally formatted clock labels in the display layer.

feedback.reason: Keep duration based on the time representation the event actually owns. In this case, Have Meeting calculate elapsed duration from its stored start and end instants.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Meeting owns the two instants that define its elapsed duration.
details.scenarioApplication: Attendees can format those same endpoints locally without changing the underlying duration.
details.errorCorrection: Across a daylight-saving transition, the displayed wall-clock difference may not equal elapsed time. That number can contradict the actual interval represented by the event.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the product asks for scheduled wall-clock hours, model that separate business quantity explicitly.
details.transfer: Choose the representation that actually defines the measure before locating its calculation.

messages.text: That number can contradict the actual interval represented by the event.
Across a daylight-saving transition, the displayed wall-clock difference may not equal elapsed time.

learningObjective: Choose how the stay should report its number of nights.

question.prompt: A hotel stay stores check-in and check-out calendar dates in the hotel’s local calendar. A stay crossing midnight counts each occupied night; time-zone conversion is not part of this contract. Choose how the stay should report its number of nights.

options.text: Have HotelStay count the hotel-local dates from check-in up to but not including check-out.
Convert both dates to the traveler’s device zone and subtract elapsed hours divided by 24.
Let each booking page decide whether check-out day is inclusive.

feedback.reason: Calculate a domain quantity from the dates and counting rule the stay owns. In this case, Have HotelStay count the hotel-local dates from check-in up to but not including check-out.

details.mechanismOrProperty: HotelStay owns the local dates and the rule that defines an occupied night.
details.scenarioApplication: The count stays stable when a traveler views the booking from another time zone.
details.errorCorrection: The prompt defines hotel-local calendar nights, not elapsed 24-hour periods. The same stay could then show different night counts on different pages.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a business adopts a different date-counting rule, represent that policy explicitly rather than hiding it in a screen.
details.transfer: Keep the calculation beside the date facts and convention that give the result its meaning.

messages.text: The prompt defines hotel-local calendar nights, not elapsed 24-hour periods.
The same stay could then show different night counts on different pages.

learningObjective: Choose how boundary membership should be evaluated consistently wherever bands are used.

question.prompt: A temperature band has inclusive lower and upper bounds. A reading belongs to the band when it is equal to either endpoint or between them. Choose how boundary membership should be evaluated consistently wherever bands are used.

options.text: Let each alert screen compare the reading against the two endpoints itself.
Store an isInside flag on each reading and update it whenever any band changes.
Have TemperatureBand answer whether a reading is within its inclusive bounds.

feedback.reason: Keep a value-object predicate with the bounds and endpoint rule it represents. In this case, Have TemperatureBand answer whether a reading is within its inclusive bounds.

details.mechanismOrProperty: TemperatureBand owns the endpoints and inclusive comparison rule.
details.scenarioApplication: Alerting and reporting callers ask the same band about a reading.
details.errorCorrection: A screen can accidentally omit equality at one endpoint, creating a different band rule. Membership then depends on stale derived state rather than the selected band.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If different alert policies require different thresholds, each band instance should carry its own stated bounds.
details.transfer: Keep a predicate with the value and rule that define the predicate.

messages.text: A screen can accidentally omit equality at one endpoint, creating a different band rule.
Membership then depends on stale derived state rather than the selected band.

learningObjective: Choose how the board should determine the number of ready tasks after a dependency is edited.

question.prompt: A project board stores tasks and dependency links. A task is ready only when all its recorded prerequisites are complete; the board can change links. Choose how the board should determine the number of ready tasks after a dependency is edited.

options.text: Have the dashboard keep its own dependency graph copy and compute readiness there.
Have ProjectBoard evaluate readiness from its current tasks and dependency links.
Let every task mark itself ready based only on its own status.

feedback.reason: Keep a graph-derived decision with the aggregate that owns the graph being evaluated. In this case, Have ProjectBoard evaluate readiness from its current tasks and dependency links.

details.mechanismOrProperty: ProjectBoard owns the collection and links whose combined state determines readiness.
details.scenarioApplication: A link edit is reflected in the next readiness calculation without asking each task to guess about the graph.
details.errorCorrection: A task cannot determine whether other recorded prerequisites are complete from its status alone. That copy can disagree with the board after a link edit.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: For very large graphs, a computed index may help, but it must be derived from the authoritative board graph.
details.transfer: Place cross-member behavior at the aggregate that has the relationships needed to decide it.

messages.text: That copy can disagree with the board after a link edit.
A task cannot determine whether other recorded prerequisites are complete from its status alone.

learningObjective: Choose how the risk band should stay aligned with reviewer edits to severity and likelihood.

question.prompt: An inspection finding stores severity and likelihood. The published risk band is the cell in a fixed matrix selected by those two values; reviewers cannot edit the band separately. Choose how the risk band should stay aligned with reviewer edits to severity and likelihood.

options.text: Have InspectionFinding select its risk band from its severity, likelihood, and the fixed matrix.
Let reviewers edit a risk label independently after changing severity.
Have each report apply its own copy of the severity matrix.

feedback.reason: Derive a classification from the attributes that determine it. In this case, Have InspectionFinding select its risk band from its severity, likelihood, and the fixed matrix.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The finding owns the two inputs and the matrix rule defines their classification.
details.scenarioApplication: A severity or likelihood correction automatically changes the computed band.
details.errorCorrection: The label can describe a different pair of inputs from the saved finding. Reports can classify the same finding differently even though the matrix is fixed by the prompt.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the matrix itself becomes versioned, capture the matrix revision with the finding.
details.transfer: Do not persist a separately editable answer to a classification that follows from owned facts.

messages.text: The label can describe a different pair of inputs from the saved finding.
Reports can classify the same finding differently even though the matrix is fixed by the prompt.

learningObjective: Choose how to keep itinerary travel time accurate when one leg is rebooked.

question.prompt: A rental itinerary stores travel legs in sequence. Its displayed travel time is the sum of each leg’s booked duration; waiting time is shown separately. Choose how to keep itinerary travel time accurate when one leg is rebooked.

options.text: Let each booking screen add the new duration to a saved total when a leg changes.
Include connection waiting time in each leg’s duration when rendering the itinerary.
Have RentalItinerary sum the booked durations of its current legs.

feedback.reason: Derive a total from the member facts and exclude quantities the contract separates. In this case, Have RentalItinerary sum the booked durations of its current legs.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The itinerary owns the current legs and their booked durations.
details.scenarioApplication: Rebooking one leg changes the total once, while separately displayed waits remain outside it.
details.errorCorrection: A canceled or replaced leg can be counted twice if a path misses the compensating update. The prompt defines waiting time as a separate quantity, so that changes the meaning of travel time.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the product later defines door-to-door journey time, add that as a distinct measure.
details.transfer: A total should follow from its actual members and the quantity’s explicit definition.

messages.text: A canceled or replaced leg can be counted twice if a path misses the compensating update.
The prompt defines waiting time as a separate quantity, so that changes the meaning of travel time.

learningObjective: Choose how the activation screen should display the deadline after a permitted edit.

question.prompt: A service window stores a start instant and an allowed duration. The deadline is start plus that duration; support staff may change either input before activation. Choose how the activation screen should display the deadline after a permitted edit.

options.text: Have the activation screen independently add a default duration to the displayed start.
Have ServiceWindow calculate its deadline from its start and allowed duration.
Keep a deadline field that support must remember to update after changing the start.

feedback.reason: Calculate a deadline from its owned start and duration rather than maintaining a conflicting copy. In this case, Have ServiceWindow calculate its deadline from its start and allowed duration.

details.mechanismOrProperty: ServiceWindow owns the inputs that define the deadline.
details.scenarioApplication: Changing a permitted input changes the displayed deadline through one rule.
details.errorCorrection: The stored deadline can cease to match the two inputs the window says define it. A different screen may use another default and show another deadline.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Once activated, if the contract freezes the deadline, capture the resulting instant as an explicit lifecycle fact.
details.transfer: Derived deadlines belong near their source values until the lifecycle explicitly captures them.

messages.text: A different screen may use another default and show another deadline.
The stored deadline can cease to match the two inputs the window says define it.

learningObjective: Choose how to show proposed ingredient quantities without changing stored batch state.

question.prompt: A compost batch stores ingredient proportions and a target quantity. Operators can request a proposed batch size; the batch is not changed until the proposal is accepted. Choose how to show proposed ingredient quantities without changing stored batch state.

options.text: Have CompostBatch calculate a proposal from its proportions and requested target without mutating itself.
Let the proposal screen overwrite the batch quantities while the operator is still reviewing.
Have the operator copy each ingredient into a calculator and manually scale it.

feedback.reason: Use an operation that evaluates owned state while keeping a proposal distinct from an accepted transition. In this case, Have CompostBatch calculate a proposal from its proportions and requested target without mutating itself.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The batch owns the proportions; a calculation can use them without committing a state change.
details.scenarioApplication: The preview can be discarded safely or accepted later through its separate transition.
details.errorCorrection: That changes accepted state before the prompt’s explicit acceptance point. The repeated calculation can use inconsistent proportions or rounding.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If proposals become independently saved records, model their own lifecycle rather than treating previews as accepted batches.
details.transfer: Cohesion includes keeping evaluation inputs together while respecting whether an operation changes state.

messages.text: That changes accepted state before the prompt’s explicit acceptance point.
The repeated calculation can use inconsistent proportions or rounding.

learningObjective: Choose how an existing case should continue to report its due instant after policy changes.

question.prompt: A support case stores its opened instant and response window. The due instant is fixed when the case is created; later policy edits affect new cases only. Choose how an existing case should continue to report its due instant after policy changes.

options.text: Recalculate the due instant from the policy currently published whenever a case is reopened.
Ask every queue and notification caller to cache its own copy of the original deadline.
Have SupportCase retain and report the due instant calculated from its captured response window at creation.

feedback.reason: Keep lifecycle-captured state with the case whose history it defines. In this case, Have SupportCase retain and report the due instant calculated from its captured response window at creation.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The case owns the creation-time response window and the resulting deadline that governs its lifecycle.
details.scenarioApplication: Policy changes apply to new cases while existing cases keep their original due instant.
details.errorCorrection: That replaces the case’s stated captured deadline with a later policy value. Independent caches can disagree or be omitted by a new caller.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A deliberate migration of open cases would be a separate explicit operation.
details.transfer: A fact that defines one object’s lifecycle should travel with that object rather than each caller.

messages.text: That replaces the case’s stated captured deadline with a later policy value.
Independent caches can disagree or be omitted by a new caller.

learningObjective: Choose how a new temperature reading should affect the zone’s heating state near the target.

question.prompt: A thermostat zone stores its target and current mode. Hysteresis keeps heating active until the measured temperature reaches the upper cutoff, rather than toggling at the target. Choose how a new temperature reading should affect the zone’s heating state near the target.

options.text: Store the previous reading in each callback instance and let callbacks decide independently.
Have ThermostatZone apply the reading using its target, mode, and hysteresis band.
Have each sensor callback turn heating off whenever the reading reaches the target.

feedback.reason: Evaluate behavior from both the new input and the owner’s prior state when the rule is stateful. In this case, Have ThermostatZone apply the reading using its target, mode, and hysteresis band.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The zone owns the target and mode whose combination defines the next state.
details.scenarioApplication: The same reading can produce different next states depending on whether the zone was already heating.
details.errorCorrection: That discards the prior mode and can cause rapid toggling inside the hysteresis band. Multiple callbacks can disagree about the zone’s current mode and cutoff behavior.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A sensor adapter can normalize units, but the zone still evaluates its state-dependent rule.
details.transfer: When a rule depends on prior state, keep the decision with the object that owns that state.

messages.text: Multiple callbacks can disagree about the zone’s current mode and cutoff behavior.
That discards the prior mode and can cause rapid toggling inside the hysteresis band.

learningObjective: Choose how the preview should recalculate sheets after paper or duplex settings change.

question.prompt: A print job stores page count, paper size, and duplex setting. A fixed estimator maps those values to sheet count; users may change the settings before submission. Choose how the preview should recalculate sheets after paper or duplex settings change.

options.text: Have PrintJob calculate its estimated sheet count from its page count, paper size, and duplex setting.
Let the preview store an independently editable sheet count next to the settings.
Have printer drivers each estimate sheets from only page count.

feedback.reason: Keep a multi-input estimate aligned with the settings from which it is derived. In this case, Have PrintJob calculate its estimated sheet count from its page count, paper size, and duplex setting.

details.mechanismOrProperty: PrintJob owns all three inputs that define the estimate.
details.scenarioApplication: Changing a setting updates the preview from the same calculation used by other consumers.
details.errorCorrection: A setting change can leave the estimate stale even though it is presented as current. They ignore the job’s selected paper or duplex state, so the number may not represent this job.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A device-specific physical estimate may be a separate collaborator if the prompt later adds device behavior.
details.transfer: Keep a result with the complete state that determines it; avoid adding a second authority.

messages.text: A setting change can leave the estimate stale even though it is presented as current.
They ignore the job’s selected paper or duplex state, so the number may not represent this job.
